title: Teenagers and Sleep
topic: สุขภาพ/ข่าว
lines: Doctors say that teenagers need about nine hours of sleep a night, but
a recent survey of 2,000 Thai high school students found that most of
**them** sleep fewer than six. The main reason is not homework, as many
parents believe. More than half of the students said they used their
phones in bed, often until after midnight.
Lack of sleep affects more than just mood. Students who slept less than
six hours scored lower in math and reading tests, and **they** were more
likely to get sick. Some schools in other countries have tried starting
classes later, at nine instead of seven-thirty. **This** gave students
nearly an hour of extra sleep, and their grades improved.
Experts suggest a simple rule: no screens for one hour before bed. "The
light from a phone tells the brain that it is still daytime," says Dr.
Pim Chai, a sleep researcher. "Without **it**, the body can relax."
